title: Project: Library Management Database
learningObjectives: Model books, members and loans as separate entities.
Use foreign keys and constraints to protect loan records.
Query current and overdue loans using date comparisons.
Record a book return without deleting loan history.
Define inventory and member-privacy tests for the project.

understand.concept: A library system tracks a catalogue, registered members and borrowing events. A loan records when a member borrowed a book and whether it has been returned.
understand.whyItMatters: Keeping loan events separate from book and member records preserves borrowing history and supports overdue reporting.
understand.analogy: A library catalogue describes books, a membership register describes borrowers, and a loan slip records each borrowing event.
understand.analogyLimit: A real library may have multiple physical copies per title, reservations, renewals, fines and branch-specific inventory; this model is intentionally compact.

explain.narrative:
## Project brief
Build a library database that stores books, members and loan events. The system must list current loans, identify overdue books and record returns while retaining historical loan data.

## ER design
Books and members are parent entities. Loans references both through foreign keys and stores loan_date, due_date and returned_at. One book can have many historical loan rows; one member can borrow many books over time.

## Business rules
A due date must follow the loan date, each loan must reference a valid book and member, and returned_at remains NULL while the loan is active. A production model should track physical copies separately from title metadata.

## Assessment and operations
Test overdue boundaries, repeat borrowing, missing members, duplicate copy loans and return updates. Restrict member personal data and document the loan policy, date/time zone and retention rules.

examples.title: Create books, members and loan events
examples.code: CREATE TABLE proj25_books (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, book_title TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE proj25_members (member_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, member_name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE); CREATE TABLE proj25_loans (loan_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES proj25_books(book_id), member_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES proj25_members(member_id), loan_date TEXT NOT NULL, due_date TEXT NOT NULL, returned_at TEXT, CHECK (due_date >= loan_date));
examples.explanation: Separates catalogue, membership and borrowing events. returned_at is NULL while the loan is active; a production schema should model individual physical copies if multiple copies exist.

examples.title: Insert sample books, members and loans
examples.code: INSERT INTO proj25_books VALUES (1, '9780000000011', 'SQL Basics'), (2, '9780000000028', 'Database Design'); INSERT INTO proj25_members VALUES (1, 'Asha', 'asha@example.test'), (2, 'Bilal', 'bilal@example.test'); INSERT INTO proj25_loans VALUES (101, 1, 1, '2026-11-01', '2026-11-15', NULL), (102, 2, 2, '2026-11-10', '2026-11-24', NULL), (103, 1, 2, '2026-10-01', '2026-10-15', '2026-10-12');
examples.explanation: Adds two titles, two members and three loan events. Loan 103 is historical because returned_at is populated.

examples.title: List currently borrowed books
examples.code: SELECT l.loan_id, b.book_title, m.member_name, l.due_date FROM proj25_loans AS l JOIN proj25_books AS b ON b.book_id = l.book_id JOIN proj25_members AS m ON m.member_id = l.member_id WHERE l.returned_at IS NULL ORDER BY l.due_date, l.loan_id;
examples.expectedOutput: 101 | SQL Basics | Asha | 2026-11-15; 102 | Database Design | Bilal | 2026-11-24
examples.explanation: Returns only active loans. Historical returned rows remain in the loan table but are excluded from the current-loan view.

examples.title: Find overdue active loans as of the stated date
examples.code: SELECT l.loan_id, b.book_title, m.member_name, l.due_date FROM proj25_loans AS l JOIN proj25_books AS b ON b.book_id = l.book_id JOIN proj25_members AS m ON m.member_id = l.member_id WHERE l.returned_at IS NULL AND l.due_date < '2026-11-22' ORDER BY l.due_date;
examples.explanation: Uses a fixed as-of date so the example is repeatable. In production, use a trusted current date/time and define the library's local time zone.

examples.title: Record a return while preserving the loan row
examples.code: UPDATE proj25_loans SET returned_at = '2026-11-20' WHERE loan_id = 101 AND returned_at IS NULL; SELECT loan_id, returned_at FROM proj25_loans WHERE loan_id = 101;
examples.explanation: Updates the active loan once and retains its history. Application code should check the affected-row count to detect an already-returned or missing loan.

practise.guidedTask: Run the current-loan and overdue queries. Return loan 101 and verify it disappears from the active-loan list while its historical row remains.
practise.independentTask: Extend the model with book_copies and reservations. Prevent the same physical copy from having two active loans and define a test for concurrent checkout attempts.
hints: Separate title metadata from loan events.
Use returned_at IS NULL to identify active loans.
Use a fixed as-of date for repeatable overdue tests.
Retain returned loans for history and reporting.
Model physical copies separately when titles have multiple copies.

questions.prompt: What does a loan row represent?
options: A borrowing event for a member and book
questions.answer: A borrowing event for a member and book
questions.explanation: Loan events should be separate from catalogue and member entities.

questions.prompt: How are current loans identified in this model?
questions.explanation: A NULL return timestamp indicates the loan is still active.

options: To preserve borrowing history and support reporting
To prevent books from being reused
questions.answer: To preserve borrowing history and support reporting
questions.explanation: Historical events are valuable for audit and library operations.

questions.prompt: Why use a fixed as-of date in the overdue example?
options: To make the expected result repeatable
questions.answer: To make the expected result repeatable
questions.explanation: Fixed dates prevent test output changing with the runtime date.

questions.prompt: What is needed when a library owns multiple copies of one title?
options: A separate physical-copy entity or copy identifier
A single book row with no copy data
A separate database for every member
questions.answer: A separate physical-copy entity or copy identifier
questions.explanation: Loan availability is tracked at copy level when several copies exist.
